reviewer.independence: Score committed before reading any prior reviews, ratings, implementation logs, or other reviewers' artifacts. Evaluated current browser UI and this game only.

rating.rationale: A complete and enjoyable close game with unusually useful legal-action and encounter guidance. The board feels coherent and card identity survives the digital adaptation. A newer player can finish a match with help from readable costs and explicit windows, but the quantity of timing decisions, repeated sidebar text, and a very compressed rules overview still impose substantial learning and pacing costs. This is a subjective interface/game-experience score, not a balance conclusion from the Runner win.

session.uiActivationCountReason: Not instrumented from the beginning. Native choices exclude local UI navigation, multi-select toggles and some queued-plan activations, so they must not be presented as mouse clicks.

method.browser: Owned new incognito preview tab; reused only my tab; browser DOM clicks and DOM reading, plus read-only public window.localTable.state/session for planning and replay capture.
method.automation: Bounded DOM-click sequences handled explicitly planned economy clicks, bioroid breaks, known cheap full-break plans and forced access/continue windows. Meaningful install, economy, run, break, trash and access choices were made by this reviewer.
limits: Single match, one side, one matchup, one desktop viewport. No multiplayer, imports, undo, mobile layout or accessibility assistive-technology study.
Read-only public snapshots were used, so this was not a purely visual novice simulation.
Final public history is bounded to 150 entries; the full 280-choice session and seed are preserved for replay.

exploration.lobby: Checked ready-made deck descriptions, identities, influence/card totals and matchup selectors. Started a new game with the requested defaults.
exploration.identity: Opened Loup's Read identity ability and read first accessed-trash reward.
exploration.deckbuilder: Opened Tune deck, inspected deck list, faction/influence totals, Ready to play state, cost curve, filters and Deckbuilding basics. Closed without saving or editing deck contents.
exploration.rules: Read How to play after game completion: win conditions, both turn structures, card inspection, gold legal-action highlights, counters and an official learning resource link.

gameNarrative: Kept Sure Gamble / Leech / Botulus / Overclock / Sure Gamble. Played both Gambles, installed Leech and challenged open HQ.
Paid 5 to Manegarm Skunkworks and trashed it for 3, triggering Loup's credit/card reward; HQ then became iced.
Installed Cleaver and probed R&D with Overclock. Whitespace was the wrong type for Cleaver and ended the run after draining the small credit pool. The UI clearly identified the mismatch.
Built a Botulus on Whitespace. At 0 credits, broke only its end-run subroutine and allowed the credit-loss subroutine to fire harmlessly, stealing Luminal Transubstantiation for 2 points.
Challenged a 4-advanced remote early in the turn and spent 3 clicks to break all three Brân 1.0 subroutines, stealing Send a Message for a 5–0 lead.

Corp scored Offworld Offices while I developed Verbal Plasticity, memory, Fermenters, Carnivore, a second hosted Botulus and later Buzzsaw. Corp purges repeatedly reset viruses; the match reached 5–6.
Used Overclock credits explicitly to break Palisade, used Carnivore multi-selection to remove Ansel from R&D and Seamless Launches from HQ, and collected Loup rewards.
Checked Archives after a concealed discard; all accessed cards were non-agendas. Continued central pressure and economic rebuilding.
Played Jailbreak targeting HQ on displayed turn 16. First random HQ access revealed Send a Message, which I stole for an 8–6 natural victory.

strengths.evidence: The encounter panel labeled Cleaver Wrong ice type at Whitespace, Botulus Hosted on different ice, Leech's effect as strength reduction rather than a break, and exact full-break credit needs. These are useful distinctions for a new Runner.
Costs appeared beside decisions, bioroid break choices explicitly cost 1 click, and Overclock's payment-source chooser offered Confirm from Overclock separately from the credit pool.

Gold available-action highlighting, separate Read card controls, source-card links, explicit multi-select counts/confirmation for Carnivore, and confirmed-choice/resource-change text made decisions reviewable.

The retained screenshot shows clearly separated blue Corp and warm Runner zones, labeled server columns, horizontal ice, a persistent grip and legible numeric counters. The presentation feels like a designed tabletop rather than a plain form.
Corp actions were narrated and could be skipped to the next decision. The entire game reached a valid terminal without reload, engine diagnostics, application crash or recovery action.
Ready-made deck plans explain the intended play style; identity text is one click away; deckbuilder shows legality, influence, cost curve, card costs and replacement controls.

problems.title: Timing confirmation volume still dominates an ordinary match
problems.reproduction: Play this recorded session. Known simple runs repeatedly require encounter pass, movement Continue the run, access/finish windows and ability selection. Session contains 132 command n records among 280 native choices.
problems.observedImpact: A rules-aware AI could keep moving, but a newer player must repeatedly decide whether a window contains a useful action. Break all reduces some work, yet a full match still feels much more procedural than its strategic turn count suggests.
problems.suggestion: Provide an optional newcomer timing mode that groups safe passes with a clear preview of what will resolve; preserve the current full-control mode. Do not equate native-choice count with actual UI clicks.

problems.title: Encounter sidebar mixes essential decisions with repeated explanations and irrelevant installed tools
problems.reproduction: With Leech, Cleaver and Botulus installed on R&D, run a different server; later install the second Botulus and inspect Palisade/Whitespace encounters. The panel lists each hosted virus even when it says Hosted on different ice, repeats explanatory copy, full-break math, confirmed choice and activity sections.
problems.observedImpact: Useful information is present, but at the 1280×800 desktop viewport it creates a long decision rail. The next movement/pass action can be visually separated from the relevant ice and tool choices.
problems.suggestion: Keep current ice, usable choices and the primary continuation action together; collapse unavailable tools and deeper explanation by default while keeping reasons discoverable.

problems.title: Rules overview explains mechanics but does not walk a new Runner through a first run
problems.reproduction: Open How to play. It provides a short role overview, counters and legal-action conventions, but no worked example of choosing a target, matching ice type/strength, breaking selected subroutines or sequencing economy before a run.
problems.observedImpact: The encounter guidance rescues local tactical decisions, but a first-time player still has to discover the larger economy/rig/run sequence by trial. My early Overclock probe failed against a code gate despite ample total starting money; that was my strategic choice, not an engine error.
problems.suggestion: Offer an optional short guided scenario or worked example alongside the existing concise overview, using a known face-up ice encounter and an economy setup step.

problems.title: Some cost labels have grammatical rough edges
problems.reproduction: At Palisade or Whitespace with an affordable full break, the button reads Break all · 1 credits. Manegarm's payment option reads Pay 5 credit.
problems.observedImpact: Meaning remains clear, but the rough labels weaken otherwise polished presentation.
problems.suggestion: Use consistent credit/credits inflection across generated action labels.

problems.title: Win screen gives little retrospective explanation of a long close game
problems.reproduction: Reach the preserved natural terminal. The primary copy is You win, Runner wins, Well played and Runner reached 8 agenda points; the rail still shows the most recent activity and last resource change.
problems.observedImpact: The ending confirms the result well, but it misses a good learning moment after a 16-turn 8–6 game.
problems.suggestion: Add a compact optional match recap with agenda steals/scores and notable turns, plus direct replay/export entry points.

automationLimitations: Initial screenshot timed out. One midgame screenshot succeeded and was inspected. Three later terminal-screenshot attempts timed out; no terminal screenshot retained.

Several DOM automation calls attempted a button before the next render, or expected a different visible label. These produced evaluator TypeErrors only; subsequent DOM reads showed a healthy game. One generic forced-action loop encountered null decision after the win. These are automation errors, not demonstrated application defects.
